answer: New identities are minted only by splitting a parent key's escrowed stake. A parent wanting a child posts half its bond, and the child's ledger entry names that parent as a mirror of its conduct: fraud proven on the child also burns the parent's remaining half. Each root divides at most twice per epoch, so a thousand aliases need dozens of funded roots, not one wallet. Operators keep a public atlas of lineage, every branch visible, and auditors verify only the root set. A farm pays per root and risks a whole tree on one bad leaf, while a clean operator still draws nectar from the shared pool.
